title: First Sitting of 2nd Session of 2025
summary: The first sitting of the second session opened at 09:02 with 39 members present. South Hulhumale' member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed raised an urgent question on the 1 June power cut across Greater Male', but members voted 9 to 43 against debating it. The chair then sent three ambassador nominations to the Foreign Relations Committee and a set of Supreme Court judge nominations to the Judiciary Committee. Debate began on the government bill amending the Civil Aviation Authority Act; speakers backed it but spent much of their time trading arguments over the power cut and over trust, and the Speaker ended the sitting at 10:06 without concluding the debate. The text layer is partly garbled, so some names and figures are less certain.

Preliminary debate on the bill to amend the Maldives Civil Aviation Authority Act (Law 2/2012), government bill presented by Dhaandhoo member Mohamed Fazeel
items.outcome: debated; Speaker ended the sitting before the debate concluded

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Raised a point of order that the bill's name should be stated at least once during debate.
Supported the amendment but said trust is the issue, citing the outage, a pending financial investigation and recent Supreme Court changes.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Presented the Civil Aviation Authority Act amendment, saying it strengthens the authority's powers, aviation safety and departure-tax auditing in line with ICAO standards.
Raised a point of order in reply to a remark by another member about the power cut.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said the amendment is modest, questioned why the aviation fee goes to the Finance Ministry rather than the authority, and called a five-hour outage unacceptable.
Argued that backup generators and emergency response at the main airport should be examined and officials held accountable.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Defended the government, saying power problems were inherited, citing the Addu and Velana airport projects, and argued earlier governments left unresolved issues.
Said the opposition has had little time in government to judge and the debt left behind shaped current priorities.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Raised an urgent question on the 1 June power cut across Greater Male', citing effects on businesses, hospitals and the airport, and asked the House to take it up.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Backed the aim of the amendment but argued the airport power cut showed a government failure, and asked for an independent investigation the public could trust.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the amendment and said he planned to propose an extra amendment on Friday prayer-time flight rules, which he said changed in 2009.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the amendment, tracing how airport taxes have been collected and arguing an island nation needs a stronger air transport system and passenger protections.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the bill and said the urgent question did not meet the rule, as power was restored within about two hours, comparing it to the 2014 water crisis.

decisions: The urgent question on the power outage was not taken up for debate (9 yes, 43 no, 52 voting, 27 needed).
Hussain Ziyad was assigned to the Judiciary Committee in place of Mauroof Zakir.
Ambassador nominations for Nepal, Ireland and Ukraine were sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
Supreme Court judge nominations were sent to the Judiciary Committee.
The Speaker closed the sitting without concluding debate on the Civil Aviation Authority Act amendment bill.
